Well pumps can require 3–5 times their normal running power for a few seconds when starting, so startup capacity is often the biggest challenge.

markup:
To run a well pump with a solar generator, you need to size it for **two things: the pump's startup surge power and how long you want it to run.**

Well pumps can require 3–5 times their normal running power for a few seconds when starting, so startup capacity is often the biggest challenge.

## Recommended solar generator sizes

These are rough estimates for common 240V well pumps.

| Well pump size | Running watts (approx.) | Startup surge (approx.) | Suggested inverter |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ½ HP | 700–1,200W | 2,000–4,000W | 4,000W |
| ¾ HP | 1,000–1,500W | 3,000–5,000W | 5,000W |
| 1 HP | 1,400–2,000W | 4,000–7,000W | 6,000W+ |
| 1.5 HP | 2,000–3,000W | 6,000–10,000W | 8,000W+ |
| 2 HP | 2,500–4,000W | 8,000–12,000W | 10,000W+ |

Actual requirements depend on the pump motor, control box, and starting method. The generator must also support the pump's voltage, usually 120V or 240V AC.

## How much battery capacity do you need?

Battery capacity determines how long you can run the pump.

For example, suppose you have a 1 HP pump consuming 1,800W while running.

| Total pump runtime per day | Energy required (including ~15% losses) |
|---|---:|
| 15 minutes | 0.53 kWh |
| 30 minutes | 1.06 kWh |
| 1 hour | 2.12 kWh |
| 2 hours | 4.24 kWh |
| 4 hours | 8.47 kWh |

A 5 kWh battery could provide roughly 2.3 hours of total pump runtime at that load, assuming the battery's full rated capacity is usable.

## Tell me about your well pump

{@body const [hp,setHp] = DIL.useState("1")}
{@body const [voltage,setVoltage] = DIL.useState("240")}
{@body const [usage,setUsage] = DIL.useState("house")}
{@body const [duration,setDuration] = DIL.useState("30")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Size a solar generator for my well pump: "+hp+" HP, "+voltage+"V, usage: "+usage+", estimated total pump runtime per day: "+duration+" minutes. Recommend inverter continuous/surge rating, battery capacity, and solar panel wattage.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>1. What horsepower is your pump?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={hp} onChange={setHp}>
        <radio value="0.5">½ HP</radio>
        <radio value="0.75">¾ HP</radio>
        <radio value="1">1 HP</radio>
        <radio value="1.5">1.5 HP</radio>
        <radio value="2">2 HP</radio>
        <radio value="unknown">Not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>2. What voltage does it use?</label>
      <radio-group direction="row" value={voltage} onChange={setVoltage}>
        <radio value="120">120V</radio>
        <radio value="240">240V</radio>
        <radio value="unknown">Not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>3. What is the well used for?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={usage} onChange={setUsage}>
        <radio value="house">Household water supply</radio>
        <radio value="irrigation">Irrigation / agriculture</radio>
        <radio value="livestock">Livestock</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>4. Estimated total pump runtime per day</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={duration} onChange={setDuration}>
        <radio value="15">15 minutes</radio>
        <radio value="30">30 minutes</radio>
        <radio value="60">1 hour</radio>
        <radio value="120">2 hours</radio>
        <radio value="unknown">Not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button submit block>Calculate my solar generator size <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

With these details, I can recommend the **inverter wattage, battery size (kWh), and solar panel capacity** you need, including whether a portable solar generator will work or you need a larger 240V system.
